function.name: search_google
function.description: Performs a search query on Google and returns a list of URLs that match the search criteria. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term to query on Google.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. The number must be a positive integer.

language.description: The language for the search results.

filter.description: A flag to filter explicit content in search results.

date_range.description: The date range for the search results in the format 'MM/DD/YYYY-MM/DD/YYYY'. If not specified, searches across all dates.

message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the world’s most prominent vaccine manufacturers (as of 2026).  The list includes companies that produce vaccines for COVID‑19, influenza, HPV, meningitis, and other diseases, as well as those that supply vaccines to global health initiatives.

| Company | Headquarters | Key Vaccines (2026) | Notable Highlights |
|---------|--------------|---------------------|--------------------|
| **Pfizer‑BioNTech** | New York, USA / Mainz, Germany | COVID‑19 mRNA (Comirnaty), HPV, RSV, influenza | First mRNA vaccine to receive WHO emergency use listing; strong global distribution network. |
| **Moderna** | Cambridge, USA | COVID‑19 mRNA (Spikevax), RSV, influenza, malaria (in development) | Rapid mRNA platform; first to roll out a booster for COVID‑19 in 2024. |
| **Johnson & Johnson (Janssen)** | New Brunswick, USA | COVID‑19 single‑dose (Ad26.COV2.S), HPV, meningococcal, influenza | Adenovirus‑vectored platform; single‑dose COVID‑19 vaccine used widely in low‑resource settings. |
| **Novavax** | Gaithersburg, USA | COVID‑19 protein subunit (Nuvaxovid), influenza, RSV | Protein‑based vaccine with high efficacy; strong safety profile. |
| **GlaxoSmithKline (GSK)** | Brentford, UK | HPV (Cervarix), influenza, RSV, pneumococcal, meningococcal | Long‑standing global vaccine portfolio; active in WHO’s Gavi partnership. |
| **Sanofi Pasteur** | Lyon, France | Influenza, meningococcal, typhoid, rabies, polio | One of the largest vaccine producers in Europe; strong presence in Africa and Asia. |
| **Merck & Co. (MSD)** | Kenilworth, USA | HPV (Gardasil‑9), influenza, COVID‑19 (mRNA‑1273‑RBD), shingles | Diversified vaccine pipeline; active in global health programs. |
| **AstraZeneca** | Cambridge, UK | COVID‑19 (ChAdOx1‑S), influenza, HPV, typhoid | Adenovirus‑vectored COVID‑19 vaccine; strong manufacturing capacity in the UK and India. |
| **Sinovac Biotech** | Beijing, China | COVID‑19 inactivated (CoronaVac), influenza, typhoid | Inactivated vaccine platform; large domestic market and export to many LMICs. |
| **Bharat Biotech** | Hyderabad, India | COVID‑19 (Covaxin), influenza, typhoid, hepatitis B | Inactivated vaccine platform; significant contribution to India’s domestic vaccine supply. |
| **CureVac** | Tübingen, Germany | COVID‑19 mRNA (CVnCoV), influenza, RSV (in development) | Focus on self‑amplifying RNA technology; early-stage pipeline. |
| **Serum Institute of India** | Pune, India | Polio, measles‑rubella, hepatitis B, influenza, COVID‑19 (Covishield) | Largest vaccine manufacturer by volume; key partner for Gavi and UNICEF. |
| **Sinopharm (China National Pharmaceutical Group)** | Beijing, China | COVID‑19 inactivated (BBIBP‑CorV), influenza, hepatitis B | Inactivated vaccine platform; major exporter to Middle East and Africa. |
| **Biontech (German subsidiary of Pfizer‑BioNTech)** | Mainz, Germany | COVID‑19 mRNA (Comirnaty), influenza (in development) | European manufacturing hub for mRNA vaccines. |
| **Bharat Biotech** | Hyderabad, India | Covaxin (COVID‑19), influenza, typhoid | Inactivated vaccine platform; significant domestic and export presence. |
| **Janssen (Johnson & Johnson)** | New Brunswick, USA | COVID‑19 single‑dose, HPV, meningococcal | Adenovirus‑vectored platform; strong presence in low‑resource settings. |
| **GSK** | Brentford, UK | HPV, influenza, RSV, meningococcal | Long‑standing global vaccine portfolio; active in WHO’s Gavi partnership. |

### How to Use This List
- **Research**: If you’re looking into vaccine supply chains, partnerships, or clinical trials, this table gives a starting point for each company’s key products.
- **Investment**: For investors, note the diversification of platforms (mRNA, adenovirus, protein subunit, inactivated) and the geographic spread of manufacturing.
- **Public Health**: For policymakers, the list highlights which manufacturers are active in WHO‑listed vaccines and which have strong presence in low‑ and middle‑income countries.

If you need deeper details—such as production capacities, R&D pipelines, or recent regulatory approvals—just let me know!
